messages:
sam: Hi team, first day question 3: I can log into Console but clicking into the prod admin UI gives me a 403. I need read access to feature flags in prod for a quick smoke test. Who should I ask and what's the fastest path?
leila: welcome Sam! For prod flag reads we typically grant `console:prod-ff-read`. If you also need to flip anything that's `console:prod-ff-toggle` which needs approvals from the flag owners + security. Ping infra with your employee id and the exact flags.
sam: my id is 11098. The flags are `payments.enable_new_flow` and `routing.low_latency_mode`. Can infra do a short-lived read grant while I wait for approvals?
leila: yes we can do a timeboxed read grant (48h) without owner sign-off. Toggles are different. Please open a ticket in #infra-access with the payload: `name: Sam R; id: 11098; env: prod; projects: payments,routing; scopes: console:prod-ff-read; duration: 48h`
sam: done, ticket created. Also saw an MFA prompt fail once. Any SSO quirks I should know?
emily: emily from devex here 3: for prod admin scopes you must be on SSO + MFA and on the corporate VPN if you're external. If MFA fails, try reauthing via the SSO portal directly, sometimes the magic-link in the Console times out.
ops-bot: [automated] Access request #INFR-4901 submitted by sam. Status: pending manual approval. Link: https://redwood.internal/infr/tickets/INFR-4901
sam: thanks. If the owners deny toggle access, is there a way to request a vetted runbook or an engineer to perform the flip for me? I only need a small canary for verification.
leila: good question. Owners can either grant toggle rights, perform the flip themselves, or ask eng-sre to run a canary per the safe-flip playbook. In urgent cases, owners can tag `@eng-sre` and request a controlled rollout.
leila: also note: for high-risk flags (billing, auth) we require a two-person approval and a rollback plan in the ticket. Payments.enable_new_flow may fall into that bucket depending on scope.
sam: understoood. One more: can service accounts be used for automated smoke tests against prod flags, or do we need human SSO?
emily: service accounts are allowed but must go through the access request for machine credentials and need a short-lived token setup. We prefer human SSO for one-off checks. For CI smoke tests use dedicated service identities with least privilege.
sam: great, thanks everyone. I'll wait for the ticket and will DM the flag owners to speed approvals. Appreciate the quick help :)
